critic_summary: Targeted failure mode: prompt-l5's Propose-Audit-Falsify-Commit method has a Step 5 #3 'weakest-violation' branch that ships the smallest-margin FALSIFIED candidate when zero candidates survive. L6/L7/L8 all hit this branch (L6 round-number, L7 streak, L8 anchor-drift) and all reverted; in every case the researcher's own NOTES.md pre-acknowledged a likely revert before shipping, and L8's trace explicitly names the missing 'refuse-to-commit' branch as the root cause. The proposed Propose-Audit-Falsify-OR-Refuse method makes three changes: (a) Step 5 #3 is replaced by a refuse-to-commit branch whose deliverable is a thin wrapper around the champion's get_execution_algorithm factory (byte-for-byte champion behavior, ties on every metric by construction) plus a structured negative-result memo with a remaining-axis-budget that names 3-5 untouched axis categories and prioritises one for the next loop; (b) HETEROGENEOUS falsification rules must now be volume-weighted (L8's equal-weighted rule hid that dense positive-delta dates dominated the aggregate, producing a worse-than-predicted pnl of $377 vs the predicted ~$754); (c) SURVIVED implementations layer on the champion rather than the parent, addressing the L7-critic-named champion-redundancy failure mode that the prompt-l5 method has no machinery for. Gate result: 0/5 metrics improved vs running-best L5 (pnl 377.25 vs 1471.75, sharpe 2.79 vs 13.72, max_dd -0.027 vs -0.016, win_rate 0.3504 vs 0.3547; mean_slippage tied at 0). Action: reverted. If the new method works, the next reasoning trace will show: a NOTES.md whose Step 5 produces either a SURVIVED-candidate champion-layered implementation or a refuse-to-commit memo with an exhausted-axis list and a single named next-axis priority; volume-weighted falsification statistics rather than equal-weighted; and a 'Where I felt uncertain' section that no longer names 'weakest-violation forced ship' or 'champion-redundancy' as the dominant uncertainty.
